## Wrap values through a callback or the layout (`periodic`) {#sec-ch11-periodic}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What it does.** Fills the ghosts of a periodic face with the owned cells at the opposite end: by an in-block
copy when the callback is still installed, or by the layout's exchange with the wrapped neighbour when the
layout owns the wrap.
**Switch.** Face name `periodic`; off by default (the default face is `reflecting`).
**Requires / implies / turns off.** A periodic x2 (x3) name sets the layout flag `periodic_x` (`periodic_y`),
which nulls the callbacks of that direction; a periodic x1 name sets `periodic_z` only on the `cubed` layout.
**Order.** An exact permutation of cell averages on a matching mesh.
**Defining equation.** @eq-ch11-periodic-copy.
:::

Periodicity is the one boundary that two different fillers can own. On a slab layout the x2 and x3 wraps are
the layout's: the periodic names set the layout flags, construction nulls the callbacks, and the exchange of
@sec-ch11-exchange copies the wrapped neighbour's cells, which on a single block are the block's own opposite
cells. The x1 wrap on a slab layout stays with the callback, which copies inside the block. On the `cubed`
layout the x1 wrap is the layout's too.

### Derivation

For a periodic field, translation by the domain length leaves its cell integral unchanged. On matched
cells the discrete boundary operation is therefore an exact permutation of cell averages, not an
interpolation. With owned cells $1,\ldots,n_1$ and ghost depth $l=1,\ldots,n_g$, the x1 callback gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
q_{1-l}&=q_{n_1+1-l},\\
q_{n_1+l}&=q_l.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch11-periodic-copy}

`periodic_inner` and `periodic_outer`
([`bc_func.cpp:36-50`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L36-L50))
implement @eq-ch11-periodic-copy as one slab copy each, with no sign change for any row.
For several blocks the donor is the wrapped neighbour that `SlabLayoutImpl::neighbor_rank`
({{< code src/layout/slab_layout.cpp SlabLayoutImpl::neighbor_rank >}}) selects by adding the block count
to a negative index or subtracting it from one past the end, and the same identity applies to the global
cell index. This proves exact copying on a matching periodic mesh, not the conservation of independently
reconstructed seam fluxes. Check C1 checks both callback copies and the repeated fill [check
`src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.out`]. The checks do
not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

The layout flag `periodic_x` refers to x2, `periodic_y` to x3 and `periodic_z` to x1
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). The card sets the first two
for periodic x2 and x3 faces; a periodic x1 face sets the third only when the layout type is `cubed`, so on a
slab layout the x1 periodic callback stays installed and copies inside the block. `MeshBlockImpl::reset`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}) nulls every callback of a direction whose layout
flag is set, and those faces are then filled at exchange time. A periodic-named callback that survives
(the slab x1 case) is physical for `is_physical_boundary`, is not an x1 wall for the hydro
(@sec-ch11-registry), and is treated as non-physical by the corner refresh of @sec-ch11-timing, which
re-applies the x1 callbacks on its slabs. No independent convergence order is associated with this exact
permutation.

: Implementation sites for periodic. {#tbl-ch11-periodic-code}

1. Parse the periodic face names and set the layout flag of the direction. The anchor `periodic_x` is in
   {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}.
2. Null the layout-owned face callbacks; keep the slab x1 callback. The anchor `bfuncs` is in
   {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}.
3. Copy the opposite owned slab in the callback, or obtain the wrapped neighbour through the layout. The
   anchor `periodic_inner` is in
   [`bc_func.cpp:36-50`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L36-L50);
   the anchor `periodic_x` of the wrap is in {{< code src/layout/slab_layout.cpp SlabLayoutImpl::neighbor_rank >}}.

: Source-defined assertions for periodic; no runtime results. {#tbl-ch11-periodic-tests}

The assertion is the top-level `assert` on the ghost strip in {{< code tests/test_mesh_exchange.py >}}; the
neighbour it compares against is the one `neighbor_rank` returns for offset $(0,1,0)$.

Numeric tolerances above are the source test constants; a round-off derivation is not documented for each.
Device/rank distinctions and missing runs are recorded in @sec-ch15-ch11.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
In-block copy and neighbour exchange are distinct paths and only the second is exercised by the exchange
test. The multi-rank exchange and positivity seam suites are inventoried in @sec-ch15-ch11; their runtime
coverage is pending. A copied donor factor must stay single-valued across its shared face; this section does
not replace the positivity analysis of @sec-ch08.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result
is claimed.
:::
